claims.text: Iodine's block is transitory (a few days to a week), then usually stops.
claims.quote: a transitory effect lasting from a few days to a week, after which inhibition usually ceases.

claims.text: It generally isn't used for routine hyperthyroidism tx;
claims.quote: Iodine generally is not used for routine treatment of hyperthyroidism.

claims.text: uses are thyroid storm, emergency nonthyroid surgery, and prep for thyroidectomy.
claims.quote: Iodine is used for emergency management of thyroid storm, for hyperthyroid patients undergoing emergency nonthyroid surgery, and (because it also decreases the vascularity of the thyroid) for preoperative preparation of patients with hyperthyroidism undergoing thyroidectomy.

claims.text: Before thyroidectomy: SSKI 3 drops (about 100–150 mg) PO TID for 10 days.
claims.quote: Saturated solution of potassium iodide 3 drops (about 100 to 150 mg) orally 3 times a day should be given for 10 days before surgery to reduce the vascularity of the gland.

claims.text: Give methimazole first; the patient should be euthyroid before iodide is given.
claims.quote: However, methimazole must be given first because the patient should be euthyroid before iodide is given.

claims.text: Thyroid storm: PTU 600 mg PO given before iodine,
claims.quote: Propylthiouracil: 600 mg orally given before iodine, then 200–400 mg every 6–8 hours

claims.text: then SSKI 5 drops (0.25 mL) PO q6h.
claims.quote: Iodine: 5 drops (0.25 mL) saturated solution of potassium iodide orally every 6 hours
